chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: The Circle Ballroom and Russell's ballroom engagements
summary: He found the Circle Ballroom very boring and lists the Savoy, Roseland, Empire and the classy Arcadia as ballrooms Russell played.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, you said that you did work for about one or two weeks with Russell's band at the Circle Ballroom.
Yeah, I did... Nothin' to talk about.
Fifty-Ninth and Eighth Avenue?
That's right.
And that was boring.
To me it was very boring. Very boring.
And you were glad when that finished.
Oh, that's the longest week I ever did in my life. That's no joke either. Boy, was that a long week.
Now,, you said Russell worked a number of ballrooms. Can you mention a few?
Well, let me see, now. He worked the Savoy. He worked the Roseland. He worked the Empire Ballroom. And he worked the Arcadia Balroom.
Now, the Empire Ballroom was at Forty-Ninth and
Broadway.
Forty-Ninth and Broadway.
The Arcadia?
And the Arcadia was at Fifty-Second or Fifty-Third Street and Broadway.
Now, you described the Arcadia. You said it was...
A beautiful ballroom. Beautiful. Three bandstands...
Do you remember the other bands that were there when you were there with Russell?
No, they always had something like a Spanish band or a White band.
Oh, I see.
Yeah. It was different altogether. It was a classy place. Yup, a real classy place.
